b_cap.crossing_note: boards at 428 and 429 lines (one open column, uniform odds): each child that crosses 430 must be valued at its clear points plus 0, and the backup equal the mean of clear points plus value

c_topout.note: the surviving pieces' values on this board are negative, so a top-out (0) beats surviving here: V extrapolates on near-dead boards. On real V boards all values were positive (min 7,651 over 928 boards of seed 13770); check d's min_child_value is the minimum over its own 200 sampled boards of that seed (also positive).

d_odds.note: self-consistency of the backup against the C++ nes_odds table; whether that table is NES-exact is Direction Phase 0's check

facts: native/rollout.hpp rollout(): a hand rollout that finds no placement for a piece (choice_.found false) returns at once with total -= rollout_death * (depth - step), so each missing placement of the remaining depth costs rollout_death.
The hand rollout() has no line-cap stop: its loop runs step < depth only, so it keeps placing and summing the hand value past 430 lines (leaf_rollout, 023's, stops at leaf_line_cap_).
The hand evaluation (value_of, eval.hpp) has no line-cap term; the lines only set the level (clear points and phase).
